discovery: Discovery of the high-confinement mode (H-mode) in magnetically confined plasmas and its explanation by sheared-flow suppression of turbulence

nominees.name: Friedrich Wagner
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics, Greifswald, Germany

nominees.name: Patrick H. Diamond
nominees.affiliation: University of California, San Diego, USA

motivation: In 1982 Friedrich Wagner and colleagues at ASDEX discovered that, above a power threshold, a tokamak plasma spontaneously bifurcates into a high-confinement state with a steep edge transport barrier, roughly doubling energy confinement. This H-mode was unexpected, robust and universal across devices, and it is now the operating basis of ITER, SPARC and every reactor design. Patrick Diamond, with co-workers, provided the physical explanation: sheared E×B flows decorrelate and suppress turbulent eddies, and turbulence can self-generate such flows (zonal flows), a paradigm of self-organization now central to plasma and geophysical turbulence. Keith Burrell's precise measurements on DIII-D established experimentally that flow shear controls the transition and internal transport barriers. Together, discovery, theory and verification turned plasma turbulence from an obstacle into something that can be controlled, a fundamental insight in nonlinear physics that made magnetic fusion energy scientifically feasible.
